title: MLB Trade Deadline 2026: Biggest Names on the Block Before the Aug. 3 Cutoff
excerpt: From two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal to closer Mason Miller, contenders are scrambling for pitching as the trade market heats up with 12 days to go.
body:
• The 2026 MLB trade deadline is set for August 3, with Tarik Skubal identified as the top trade target.
  • Padres closer Mason Miller is available, attracting interest from the Yankees and Mariners.
  • The Angels are open to trading shortstop Zach Neto, who has three years of control remaining.
  • The Mets are selling expiring contracts while the Yankees are in search of a catcher due to injuries.

  • Angels are surprisingly open to trading shortstop Zach Neto, who has three years of control left.
  • Mets are selling expiring contracts while Yankees seek a catcher due to injuries.

The Market Takes Shape

The 2026 MLB trade deadline arrives Monday, Aug. 3, at 6 p.m. ET — the latest possible date under the league's revised scheduling window — and the trade market is already open for business.

The Astros fired the first shot by sending veteran right-hander Lance McCullers Jr. to the first-place Milwaukee Brewers (63-37), signaling that sellers are ready to deal, according to USA Today. With the Brewers and Los Angeles Dodgers (63-38) perched atop the overall standings, contenders across both leagues are scrambling for arms.

Skubal: The Name That Looms Over Everything

Detroit's Tarik Skubal remains the single biggest domino yet to fall. The two-time Cy Young winner is a free agent after this season, and every Tigers loss intensifies the debate in Detroit about whether to cash in now or ride him into October. Detroit entered the week six games back in the AL Central and 3.5 games out of a wild card spot.

"They are ultimately going to have to weigh keeping Skubal over acquiring the wealth of prospects that will be thrown at them."

— USA Today

Beyond Skubal, starters Freddy Peralta, Sonny Gray, Sandy Alcantara, and Kevin Gausman have surfaced in trade talks. Relievers Mason Miller, Aroldis Chapman, and Ryan Helsley are also drawing interest.

Miller 'Definitely Available' — Padres Looking to Deal

Among relievers, Padres closer Mason Miller has become the market's most talked-about name. ESPN's Jeff Passan told "The Pat McAfee Show" that Miller is "definitely available," though the asking price will be steep, the New York Post reported.

Miller has been dominant in 2026 — posting a 0.89 ERA with 75 strikeouts in 39 games — just a year after San Diego acquired him from the Athletics. But the Padres, whose farm system ranks dead last in baseball, are dealing with a battered rotation. Yu Darvish, Joe Musgrove, and Nick Pivetta are all sidelined with arm injuries, while fill-in starters Walker Buehler, Griffin Canning, and Germán Márquez each carry ERAs above 5.00.

Passan identified the Seattle Mariners and New York Yankees as potential landing spots, according to the Post. "If you're a team like the Seattle Mariners that has a deep rotation already in Ryan Sloan and Kade Anderson," Passan said, "two of the best pitching prospects in baseball on the cusp of being ready for the big leagues, it's something you have to consider."

Angels Surprise by Opening the Door on Zach Neto

In one of the deadline's biggest surprises, the Los Angeles Angels are entertaining trade offers for 25-year-old shortstop Zach Neto, according to Passan and ESPN's Kiley McDaniel, as reported by the New York Post.

"The Angels are at the very least listening. Which is more than they've done at past deadlines, and 25-year-old Neto is an awfully intriguing option when Jeremy Pena's and CJ Abrams' availability at shortstop is in question."

— Jeff Passan and Kiley McDaniel, ESPN

Neto owns a career 14.4 WAR with 77 home runs, 219 RBIs, and 74 stolen bases across 465 games, with three years of club control remaining. Interim GM John Mozeliak, who replaced Perry Minasian, appears more willing to deal than his predecessor. If moved, Neto could fetch an enormous return to jumpstart the Angels' 23rd-ranked farm system.

Mets in Full Sell Mode; Yankees Shopping for a Catcher

The Mets (42-58), despite the second-highest payroll in baseball at $380 million, have declared open season on expiring contracts, per Athlon Sports. Starter Freddy Peralta (4.66 ERA, expiring deal), relievers Brooks Raley and A.J. Minter, and outfielder Tyrone Taylor are all expected to be dealt. Reliever Luke Weaver, who has allowed just one earned run since May 1 and ranks third among qualified relievers in win probability added, could also move — though New York may hold him as a bullpen anchor for 2027.

The Mets have deemed Juan Soto, Christian Scott, and three other players untouchable, according to Athlon Sports.

Meanwhile, the Yankees (55-44) are in the market for a right-handed-hitting catcher to offset injuries to Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton, and Max Fried. Potential targets include Ryan Jeffers (Twins), Hunter Goodman (Rockies), and Shea Langeliers (Athletics).

What's Next

The next 12 days will define the 2026 pennant race. A cluster of .500 teams that have not decided whether to buy or sell sits in the muddled middle of the standings, and that group is where the most unpredictable action figures to unfold. Position players like Rafael Devers, Willy Adames, Luis Arraez, and Ketel Marte have also been linked to trade rumors, making this one of the deepest deadline markets in years.
